newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr as demand peters out.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr as demand peters out.

text.p: The Indian rupee moved up on lack of demand in late trade to end Friday at 35.85/86 per dollar, dealers said. It opened the day at 35.89/91.
Dealers said the rupee traded at a high of 35.855 and a low of 35.905 per dollar on a day marked by two-way movement.
"The rupee moved up, then lost ground on demand before rallying as demand eased," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
Dealers said most of the day's trade was between 35.87 and 35.90 with only light volumes at lower levels.
"There was dollar selling from 35.90 and the rupee appreciated to 35.87, despite buying from a large state-run bank," said a dealer.
"But at around 35.87 the bank went out of the market, volumes dipped and the rupee drifted up gently to 35.855," he said.
Dealers said the rupee was steady against the forward dollar in quiet trade on Friday. They said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rolled over December-maturity swaps.
"RBI came into the market in the afternoon but was there in a limited way," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
The premia on six-month dollars ended Friday at an annualised 7.48 percent against Thursday's close of 7.52 percent, dealers said.
